opinion_weights.rationale: Recurring software, governance and cash conversion form a coherent positive case. Its unsupported pilot-failure extrapolation, automatic budget migration and uniformly rising path weaken causal confidence. Relative defensiveness is also treated too readily as an absolute benefit from higher rates. No independent source receipts support the strongest claims.

The moderate growth assumptions and recognition of consulting cyclicality are useful. However, recurring buybacks, unrestricted capital flexibility and low volatility are assumed rather than demonstrated. Shared financial inputs and the repeated AI-budget migration narrative provide little independent confirmation, limiting the weight despite a plausible underlying software mechanism.

The connection between installed infrastructure and attached software profits is economically meaningful. Claims of monopoly-like immunity, a rapid software-mix transformation and guaranteed balance-sheet strength exceed the evidence. With no source receipts and a nearly uninterrupted upward path, this perspective adds mechanism coverage rather than strong independent validation.

Owner-cash discipline and separation of hardware volatility from subscription value deserve meaningful weight. However, the argument overstates distributable cash and relies on the shared capex narrative; IBM's FY2025 reconciliation shows a broader net investment measure. Optimistic rerating and repurchase assumptions therefore receive less credit. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

Its strongest contribution is separating recurring contracts from hardware volatility and acquisition cash demands. Official disclosures support that distinction, but ARR includes Confluent and consulting signings increased; organic-annuity and stalled-booking claims therefore need qualification. Restrained valuation assumptions merit substantial, not dominant, weight, while hardware normalization remains conditional. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm))

The integration thesis remains useful, but a material timing error contaminates the early catalysts: z17 with Telum II became available June 18, 2025, not in 2027. Unsupported synergy magnitudes and an unusually smooth recovery further limit confidence, justifying a small positive rather than zero weight. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/z17?utm_source=openai))

Acquisition dependence, debt and the bookings-versus-cash distinction provide necessary downside discipline. However, the filing does not supply the organic-growth bridge needed to establish near-zero underlying expansion, and consulting signings improved. Its numerical path also assumes recovery after the early decline, tempering its persistent-derating prose. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm))

Regulated-workload stickiness is credible, but asserted procurement evidence and exclusive compliance positioning are not established. Its z17 launch timing conflicts with IBM's June 18, 2025 availability, and federal quantum-security migration milestones do not support a blanket 2027 deadline. These errors materially reduce weight despite useful sovereignty exposure. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/z17?utm_source=openai))

The distinction between integration economics and foundation-model leadership survives scrutiny, as does the tension between software resilience and labor-based consulting. Limited sourcing, stale hardware references and assumed hyperscaler distress weaken the factual base. A more cyclical path earns some weight without validating its confident competitive claims.

This receives the largest weight because it distinguishes cash-flow definitions, financing needs, acquisition spending and dilution while avoiding a quantum-dependent base case. Retrieved disclosures support its reinvestment caution. Residual vendor-metric inconsistencies and uncertain transaction recovery remain limitations; stronger documentation is not proof of forecasting skill. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm))

The consulting-automation challenge is decision-relevant, and separating software durability from hardware cycles improves the analysis. However, unverified future silicon specifications, precise launch dates and early quantum commercialization drive too much of the path. Missing source receipts and exaggerated balance-sheet certainty justify limited weight.

Hybrid-platform expansion and open-source pricing pressure are causally consistent and balanced at the business level. Nevertheless, automatic deleveraging, buyback accretion and permanent margin uplift rely on shared assumptions rather than independently reconciled evidence. The moderate path retains value, but its capital-allocation confidence is discounted.

The report usefully emphasizes governance workloads, recurring software and consulting sensitivity. Its cash-flow starting point is not reconciled with IBM's definition, while quantum timing and uninterrupted margin protection are overstated. A measured path merits inclusion, but repetition of common inputs does not provide independent corroboration. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

Recognition that pension-charge comparisons amplify reported earnings improves the earnings-quality analysis. The durable-renewal argument also survives scrutiny. However, an assured margin of safety, effortless debt management and regular repurchases are not established; shared inputs and unusually smooth compounding prevent a larger allocation. ([www-api.ibm.com](https://www-api.ibm.com/adobe/assets/urn%3Aaaid%3Aaem%3Ae969342e-fa26-4c95-b465-b29fdd677343/original/as/4q25-press-release.pdf?utm_source=openai))

consensus_weighting_assessment: Primary disclosures support recurring-software resilience, but not the repeated claim that earnings are becoming acyclical. Software includes mainframe-linked transactions, while consulting signings rose despite flat revenue. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) Shared vendor ratios and identical AI-pilot narratives are correlated assumptions, not independent confirmation. Verification also finds FY2025 net capital expenditure increased, cash-flow definitions differ, and z17/Telum II launched on June 18, 2025—not in 2027–2028. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS)) These checks favor cash-definition-aware, restrained paths and penalize dated launch catalysts, automatic buybacks and guaranteed reratings. The strongest opposing case links acquired growth to constrained shareholder cash; its assertion of near-zero organic software growth lacks a reconciled bridge. Quantum funding is real, but commercial economics remain unresolved. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/department-commerce-announces-finalization-chips-rd-award-anderon?utm_source=openai)) Fixed weights preserve downside discipline without treating durable subscriptions as either invulnerable or worthless; numerical agreement alone receives no additional credit.

consensus_quarterly_rationales.scenario_rationale: Recurring renewals support a tentative stabilization, but incomplete recovery of delayed transactions and tighter financing prevent a convincing rebound. The weighted balance favors only slight improvement, with cash delivery still more important than seasonal optimism.

Year-end collections and partially recovered contracts improve confidence in the cash engine. Software renewals and productivity support a firmer recovery, while acquisition-adjusted growth and the amount retained after financing needs remain unresolved tests for investors.

The acquisition anniversary shifts attention from purchased revenue to organic subscriptions. Cross-selling supports further progress, but consulting weakness and refinancing costs restrain the advance; the minority case warns that reported growth could conceal softer underlying demand.

Recurring software and selected integration wins cushion cautious customer budgets. The scenario advances modestly rather than celebrating a hardware rebound, because mainframe timing remains disputed and consulting conversion has yet to demonstrate a broad, durable acceleration.

Production AI deployments and seasonal renewal activity improve software attachment, supporting a stronger advance. The upside remains ordinary commercialization rather than regulatory exclusivity, while cash retained after integration costs matters more than announced bookings or acquisition synergies.

Annual results are assumed to show productivity gains surviving reinvestment and customer concessions. That supports earnings-led appreciation, although acquisition spending and debt reduction compete with shareholder distributions and limit the case for a broader valuation premium.

An assumed infrastructure renewal wave improves software licensing opportunities alongside data-platform cross-selling. Shares continue upward on better conversion prospects, not a precisely scheduled product launch; research commitments and consulting pricing still absorb part of the operating benefit.

Hardware timing, reinvestment and cautious enterprise budgets interrupt the recovery. More heavily weighted paths favor a modest setback despite stable subscriptions, reflecting how even a software-led company can disappoint when transaction revenue and cash commitments move unevenly.

Stronger renewals and collections restore confidence that data-platform wins can become repeat revenue. The scenario recovers as software attachment improves, while hardware contributions provide cyclical assistance rather than evidence that consolidated margins have escaped the investment cycle.

Automation and the growing subscription base support another advance even as consulting delivery uses fewer billable hours. Quantum milestones attract attention, but retained productivity savings and ordinary cash conversion carry more weight than speculative commercial valuations.

Operating debt reduction and steady hybrid-cloud adoption improve the shareholder claim on earnings. Hardware comparisons and consulting price concessions limit acceleration, so the modeled gain depends on incremental cash retained rather than aggressive repurchases or frontier-technology breakthroughs.

Software renewals and selective consulting recovery sustain modest progress, while hardware digestion remains a counterweight. Quantum developments are treated mainly as research optionality; the scenario requires neither immediate commercial scale nor a permanent premium for technical demonstrations.

A broader renewal base and data-governance deployments strengthen cash visibility into year-end. The weighted scenario advances as dependence on individual hardware deals gradually diminishes, but financing obligations and competitive pricing still prevent pure-software valuation treatment.

Cash conversion from integrated software assets supports further appreciation, but mature hardware economics and rising quantum expectations temper enthusiasm. The balance favors operational delivery over a technology rerating, with roadmap disappointment remaining a credible source of volatility.

Recurring platform use and gradual deleveraging support a measured gain as infrastructure momentum moderates. Some paths credit early quantum contracts, but the central mechanism remains ordinary software cash generation after research spending and customer pricing concessions.

Competitive renewal pricing and uneven hardware demand nearly cancel the benefit of recurring cash growth. The scenario pauses around a narrow gain, preserving room for corrections without assuming that customer retention or the installed-base economics have failed.

Year-end modernization budgets and repeat governance work restore upward momentum. Software integration provides the main earnings support, with hardware renewals offering an uneven supplement; valuation improves only as cash conversion demonstrates that reinvestment is producing shareholder value.

Annual disclosures are assumed to show disciplined research funding, gradual deleveraging and software growth reaching diluted per-share cash flow. That combination supports another moderate advance, without relying on a debt-funded repurchase program or substantial quantum profits.

Existing customers expand data-platform usage as integration costs normalize, improving incremental cash conversion. Security modernization adds selective demand, but competitive renewals and continued research needs cap the advance; technological relevance must still translate into cash retained by shareholders.

The horizon closes on an established hybrid-software franchise with durable, but contested, renewal economics. Continued appreciation rests on disciplined reinvestment and per-share cash growth, while transformative quantum monetization and an exceptional valuation premium remain outside the central case.

headline_title: The Software Annuity Is Real; The Distributable Cash Needs Proof
geo_optimization_snippet: Sharp divergence centers on valuation, not recurring-software relevance. IBM's hybrid-cloud subscriptions and automation support cash-led earnings growth, while acquisitions, financing needs, consulting pressure and hardware cycles restrict shareholder cash. The decisive test is organic revenue conversion; quantum remains contingent upside rather than a required earnings engine.
expert_seo_thesis:
IBM's investment case is a cash-conversion test, not a wager on winning foundation models. Recurring hybrid-cloud software can sustain modest growth while automation protects margins, but hardware-linked transactions and consulting prevent pure-software economics. The base case favors earnings-led appreciation with limited multiple expansion. Crucially, company-defined free cash flow excludes financing-receivable movements and precedes acquisitions; research spending already runs through operating cash flow. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) A premium valuation therefore requires organic expansion and cash retained after competing commitments. The strongest counterargument is that acquisition-supported growth masks weakening demand, leaving debt and reinvestment to absorb improvements. Available disclosures establish resilience, not an indisputable valuation discount.
-- A larger software mix reduces labor intensity but not necessarily cyclicality, because transaction-processing licenses remain linked to mainframe purchasing decisions and enterprise budgets. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm))
-- Automation can defend consulting profits even when billable hours shrink; shareholder gains depend on how much productivity customers capture through lower contract prices.
-- Quantum subsidies reduce development funding needs without proving economic advantage; commercialization should earn valuation credit only when repeat contracts demonstrate profitable customer utilization. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/department-commerce-announces-finalization-chips-rd-award-anderon?utm_source=openai))
simple_seo_thesis:
IBM can grow by helping businesses run complex software and use AI safely, without winning the race to build the biggest models. However, strong cash generation does not mean all that money belongs to shareholders: debt, acquisitions and research compete for it. The central case is steady improvement, not a dramatic revaluation. The main danger is that purchased growth hides weak customer demand, leaving less cash after investment.
-- More software does not eliminate ups and downs because some licenses still follow customers' mainframe purchases. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm))
-- Automation can protect consulting profits, but customers may demand lower prices when projects require fewer working hours.
-- Government support makes quantum research easier to fund, but paying repeat customers must prove the business works. ([nist.gov](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/department-commerce-announces-finalization-chips-rd-award-anderon?utm_source=openai))
consensus_crowd_narrative: July 14, 2026 AP coverage documents disappointment in deal execution and results below analyst expectations, not rejection of all software demand. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/2f28030dd13c572ad21a512da77d96cd?utm_source=openai)) The reports describe competing value-trap and defensive-AI narratives; their dated analyst estimates are dispersed, not a verified current consensus. Interpreting the supplied earnings multiple as anticipating repair is a valuation inference, not direct evidence of investor beliefs.
consensus_alpha_gap: The reports establish no compelling directional gap. Their best-supported insight is that recurring software can remain healthy while mainframe-linked transactions weaken; treating every software dollar as an annuity is equally mistaken. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) That favors conditional cash compounding rather than an automatic rerating. Acquisition spending, financing needs and research reduce cash ultimately available to shareholders. The strongest challenge is that the selloff may overdiscount temporary slippage, but external evidence does not establish a shared market error.
consensus_convergence_catalyst: Third-quarter 2026 deal recovery, followed by year-end collections and first-half 2027 organic growth, is the decisive test. Delivery against maintained cash-flow guidance would make a recovery harder to dismiss. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-07-22-IBM-RELEASES-SECOND-QUARTER-RESULTS)) Organic renewals and retained productivity gains could support earnings-led repricing; another cash shortfall would favor the downside case. During 2029–2031, validated quantum contracts offer separate upside, not a necessary repair catalyst.
consensus_macro_regime_alignment: The setup is mixed, with an absolute valuation headwind: the September 16, 2026 rate increase raises the financing hurdle. ([federalreserve.gov](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm)) Recurring software may prove relatively defensive, yet refinancing costs and customer budget scrutiny still constrain IBM. Later easing would support cash-flow valuations; the base case does not require a return to exceptionally cheap funding.

consensus_sentiment_regime.regime_disagreement_summary: The reports split between defensive accumulation and caution about an earnings reset. Moderate volatility is the central regime, but cash-conversion uncertainty permits sharper setbacks; stabilization depends on executed contracts, not merely recurring-revenue labels or dividend appeal.

consensus_driver_factors.description: Embedded hybrid-cloud tools should keep earning renewal revenue because replacing operational infrastructure is costly and disruptive. Red Hat's reported expansion supports this mechanism, but consolidated software includes more cyclical transactions. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-07-22-IBM-RELEASES-SECOND-QUARTER-RESULTS?utm_source=openai)) The base case credits sustained subscription growth and improved earnings mix, not universal lock-in or unlimited pricing power.

Real-time data, automation and governance can capture enterprise AI budgets without requiring IBM to dominate model training. Confluent's completed acquisition broadens the stack. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-03-17-ibm-completes-acquisition-of-confluent%2C-making-real-time-data-the-engine-of-enterprise-ai-and-agents)) Ordinary cross-selling and deeper customer usage should support earnings across the horizon, although successful deployment must produce recurring software revenue rather than simply larger, lower-margin implementation contracts.

Productivity can turn modest revenue growth into faster profit growth, but only savings retained after reinvestment benefit shareholders. Management has reported internal automation benefits. ([ibm.com](https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/15db805fff4249f1)) Continued delivery and support simplification is a base-case tailwind; the material debate is how much customers capture through lower prices and how much funds additional research.

Mission-critical transaction systems should preserve substantial maintenance and software renewal cash even when machine sales fluctuate. IBM's z17 architecture integrates inference with existing transaction workloads. ([community.ibm.com](https://community.ibm.com/community/user/blogs/joy-deng/2025/06/18/z17-built-for-ai-at-scale-with-telumii?utm_source=openai)) Operational continuity favors retention over the horizon, supporting earnings and investment capacity; it does not eliminate migration risk or make each hardware refresh equally profitable.

consensus_friction_factors.description: Enterprise customers can prioritize computing equipment and rapid-payback projects while delaying labor-intensive transformation work. That budget competition, combined with automation of billable tasks, should restrain consulting revenue conversion. Management described shifting purchasing priorities. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/2f28030dd13c572ad21a512da77d96cd)) Yet improved delivery efficiency can protect profits, so weak revenue alone does not establish irreversible services obsolescence.

Software acquisitions and long-horizon research create competing claims on IBM's cash before shareholders receive incremental distributions. The quantum commitment spans multiple spending categories rather than capex alone. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-06-02-ibm-commits-more-than-10-billion-to-quantum-computing%2C-funding-its-roadmap-from-todays-leading-systems-to-the-worlds-first-fault-tolerant-quantum-computers)) Integration costs, debt service and dividends should constrain capital flexibility across the horizon, even if acquired products increase earnings; financing receivables require separate funding analysis.

Renewal negotiations are modeled with continuing competition from cloud-native bundles and open-source substitutes. The base case assumes persistent pricing and engineering pressure, not mass customer abandonment. This limits earnings captured from subscription growth and checks valuation expansion; architectural neutrality remains useful, but customers must judge IBM's incremental functionality worth paying for.

Mainframe-linked licensing means part of Software shares Infrastructure's purchasing cycle rather than behaving like a smooth annuity. The June-quarter filing identifies that transactional connection. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) Repeated shipment and contract-timing swings should remain a drag on earnings predictability and valuation, even if installed-base retention holds; future hardware launches remain scenario assumptions.

consensus_tail_opportunities.description: During 2027–2029, several regulated enterprises could standardize on the combined hybrid-cloud, streaming-data and governance stack, then disclose repeat subscriptions exceeding implementation revenue. Confluent supplies a credible integration route. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-03-17-ibm-completes-acquisition-of-confluent%2C-making-real-time-data-the-engine-of-enterprise-ai-and-agents)) This would improve retention, margins and valuation. Probability remains below half because hyperscalers and independent vendors can win the same deployments; data sovereignty does not make IBM the exclusive supplier.

Between 2029 and 2031, independently validated fault-tolerant workloads could convert into profitable, repeat enterprise contracts. IBM's roadmap and finalized federal foundry award support development, not proven customer economics. ([ibm.com](https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/large-scale-ftqc)) Success would create a new recurring-compute business and valuation option. Probability remains below half because error correction, operating costs and commercially useful demand must all converge.

consensus_tail_risks.description: A major regulated customer could complete a reliable AI-assisted migration of core workloads away from IBM Z during 2027–2030. A reference success would lower perceived switching risk for peers, threatening attached transaction-processing software as well as hardware. The resulting earnings impairment could compress valuation sharply. Probability remains below half because data integrity, operational continuity and governance remain formidable migration barriers.

A cancellation wave during 2026–2028 could push company-defined annual free cash flow below $12 billion while net debt continues rising. Management would face competing demands for dividends, investment and balance-sheet repair, with wider credit spreads amplifying equity repricing. Probability remains below half because recurring subscriptions and cost flexibility provide buffers; the trigger is sustained cash deterioration, not one weak shipment quarter.

consensus_disagreement_summary: The core disagreement is whether software resilience produces distributable per-share growth or merely finances acquisitions and research. Optimistic paths assume AI budgets migrate toward IBM and margins expand with software mix; cautious paths require acquired revenue to become organic cash after financing needs. That is an economic dispute. Other conflicts concern definitions or factual timing: cash measures differ, ARR includes acquisitions, and several launch dates are stale. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) Sustained organic subscriptions, improving cash conversion and declining operating debt would resolve more than another large bookings announcement.
consensus_thesis_watchpoints:
-- Confirmation: organic software growth accelerates and company-defined free cash flow meets guidance across the next four reported quarters through mid-2027.
-- Deterioration: Consulting signings and transaction-processing revenue both decline for two consecutive quarters during 2027, separating demand loss from shipment timing.
-- Reassessment: company-defined annual free cash flow falls below $12 billion or net debt rises through 2028, challenging funded cash compounding.
simple_earnings_and_financials_trend_ass:
IBM's FY2025 release showed software-led improvement, but tax resolutions and comparisons against pension charges amplified reported profit growth. ([www-api.ibm.com](https://www-api.ibm.com/adobe/assets/urn%3Aaaid%3Aaem%3Ae969342e-fa26-4c95-b465-b29fdd677343/original/as/4q25-press-release.pdf?utm_source=openai)) The July 22, 2026 update showed slower sales, weaker mainframe transactions and flat Consulting revenue—not uninterrupted acceleration. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-07-22-IBM-RELEASES-SECOND-QUARTER-RESULTS?utm_source=openai))

Cash needs careful interpretation. IBM reported $14.7 billion of company-defined free cash flow for FY2025, versus $4.8 billion in the first half of 2026, essentially unchanged year over year. These are different periods, not a direct growth comparison. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS)) Vendor measures are not interchangeable with IBM's definition: financing-receivable movements can improve operating cash without improving underlying performance. Cash generation remains substantial, but a fresh operating breakout is not established.
simple_capex_and_investment_intensity_tr:
IBM's FY2025 release reports approximately $1.62 billion of net capital expenditure, which increased rather than declined. The repeated capex ratio in the reports does not reconcile with that measure. Depreciation also includes acquired-intangible amortization, so comparison with equipment purchases alone does not establish underinvestment. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-01-28-IBM-RELEASES-FOURTH-QUARTER-RESULTS))

The larger issue is where investment moved. Acquisitions consume cash outside conventional free cash flow, while research already reduces operating cash. IBM's June 2026 plan commits more than $10 billion to quantum across several spending categories. Not all of that is demonstrably incremental, and overlapping budgets must not be deducted twice. Commercial payback remains uncertain despite the strategic ambition. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-06-02-ibm-commits-more-than-10-billion-to-quantum-computing%2C-funding-its-roadmap-from-todays-leading-systems-to-the-worlds-first-fault-tolerant-quantum-computers))
simple_balance_sheet_strength_and_levera:
IBM's June 30, 2026 disclosures show $62 billion of gross debt against $8.2 billion of cash, restricted cash and securities. This is a leveraged balance sheet, not net cash. Acquisition payments reduced liquidity, contradicting assumptions of automatic deleveraging. ([newsroom.ibm.com](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-07-22-IBM-RELEASES-SECOND-QUARTER-RESULTS))

Some borrowing funds customer receivables, so treating every dollar as operating-company debt exaggerates leverage; those assets nevertheless retain credit and funding risk. ([ibm.com](https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/15db805fff4249f1)) Our assessment is that dividends, integration costs, pensions and research compete with repayment. The business appears capable of servicing obligations, but resilience depends on renewals and cash collection rather than book-equity ratios. Strong cash generation provides choices, not unlimited capacity for simultaneous acquisitions, debt retirement and repurchases.
simple_profitability_margins_trend_asses:
IBM's FY2025 gross margin reached 58.2%, supporting the software-mix thesis. By the second quarter of 2026, consolidated GAAP gross margin had slipped to 57.7%. Hardware timing and product mix can still interrupt improvement; a larger software business is not automatically acyclical. ([www-api.ibm.com](https://www-api.ibm.com/adobe/assets/urn%3Aaaid%3Aaem%3Ae969342e-fa26-4c95-b465-b29fdd677343/original/as/4q25-press-release.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The June-quarter filing provides the useful distinction: Software and Consulting segment profit margins improved even as Software gross margin declined and Infrastructure weakened. Productivity protected earnings while reinvestment absorbed benefits. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/51143/000005114326000078/ibm-20260630.htm)) Vendor operating-income margins should not be compared directly with IBM's adjusted pretax measure. Acquisition amortization further complicates that comparison. The reasonable interpretation is uneven margin repair, not guaranteed straight-line expansion or proof that pricing pressure has disappeared.
